newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plessey surges on Lucent tie-up talk.
newsitem.headline: Plessey surges on Lucent tie-up talk.

text.p: Shares in South African electronics firm Plessey Corp Ltd surged over 12 percent in busy trade on Wednesday on speculation that it would announce a deal with U.S.-based Lucent Technologies Inc, dealers said.
Lucent, together with France's Alcatel Altech Telecoms, on Tuesday won a two billion rand radio systems contract from South African state telecommunications utility Telkom.
Plessey on Wednesday released a cautionary on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's equities trading system, JET, that it was in unspecified talks which could have an effect on its share price.
A Plessey spokesman said that an announcement would be made at 1400 GMT but declined to give further details.
By 1100 GMT Plessey shares were up 106 cents or 12.5 percent to 950 cents, the best level in six weeks after 1.22 million shares worth over 10.0 million rand had traded.
"It is known that Plessey has been talking to Lucent for some time," one dealer said, adding that the whole electronics sector had been boosted by the deal.
The electronics index earlier touched a new life high of 4,100.5, but had since edged off its peaks.

Business Day newspaper said that Lucent, which is the unbundled arm of U.S. telecommunications firm AT&T Corp, had a distribution agreement with South African Spescom Electronics's black empowerment unit Spescom Global Systems.

Alcatel Altech, is jointly owned by South Africa's Allied Technologies Ltd (Altech) and Alcatel CIT of France. Last month black empowerment group Rethabile bought a 20 percent stake in Alcatel Altech for 125 million rand.

Spescom shares earlier touched a 830 cents day high, a gain of 20 cents in moderate volume. Altech shares jumped to a year best of 125.50 rand but had since fallen back to 111.00 rand in light volume profit-taking, dealers said.

The two year Telkom contract, which covers the supply, planning and installation of standalone telecommunications systems, will enable the provision of more than 400,000 new telephone services to customers in mainly rural and under-serviced areas.

Both Alcatel and Lucent had agreed to manufacture a significant portion of the equipment in South Africa and to seek out strategic partnerships and subcontracts with local black empowerment firms, Telkom said.
